title: Annotatio II §.VIII: Scotus and Durandus (1320) tolerate revival; Aquinas not to be dragged in
pass_a_gloss: Not disapproved by some Scholastics, especially Scotus the subtle doctor at the start of the 14th century, and the most famous Durandus in the year 1320 — whose testimonies read in Francis Foris Otrokocsi’s Irenicum ch. 6 §§.27ff. — not likewise Thomas Aquinas, who is by no means rightly dragged into Consent here by Dorsche, although he is introduced as having confessed Transubstantiation cannot be proved from the Institution words.
pass_b_english: Some Scholastics did not reject the revival — Scotus early in the 14th century, and Durandus in 1320 (Otrokocsi, Irenicum VI.27ff.).
Aquinas is not to be dragged into this consent by Dorsche, even if he grants Transubstantiation is not proved from the Institution words alone.
source_text: Non-improbata Scholasticis nonnullis, sigillatim Scoto, subtili doctori, initio seculi XIV, famosissimoque Durando, Anno 1320, quorum testimonia lege apud Franciscum Foris Otrokocsi in Irenico Cap. 6. §. 27. & seq. non item Thomæ Aquinati, à Dorschæo, hoc locô, neutiquam in Consensum trahi merito, quanquam fassus introducatur Transsubstantiationem ex verbis Institutionis probari haud posse.

lemmas.gloss: Aquinas not to be dragged in
